displayName.description: A human label. Nothing branches on it — the team's identity is `metadata.name`.

features.description: What this team is entitled to, per feature.

dwocPin.description: This team's `dwoc-pin` catalogue and default, per RFC 0002.

catalog.description: This team's catalogue entries, merged into the cluster catalogue at resolution.

items.description:
One entry of `spec.features.dwocPin.catalog`. Serializes flat, as `{key, name, namespace}`
per the RFC's own examples — not `{key, target: {name, namespace}}`.

key.description: The short identifier a grant, an annotation, or a resolved decision names.

default.description: The entry a namespace of this team gets when it names none.

endpointAuth.description: This team's `endpoint-auth` catalogue and default, per RFC 0009.

catalog.description: This team's access profiles, merged into the cluster catalogue at resolution.

items.description: One catalogue entry: what a key means.

anonymous.description: No authentication at all. `delegation` is rejected on an anonymous entry.

delegation.description: Who else, besides the owner, this profile lets in.

items.description:
Who, besides the owner, a profile may let in. A list rather than a mode, per RFC 0009: `[]`
says "the owner and nobody else" where an unquoted `Off` is YAML 1.1's boolean `false`.

key.description: The key a grant, an annotation or a path rule names.

default.description:
The key an endpoint of this team resolves to when it names none. Singular: an endpoint
resolves to exactly one profile.

imagePolicy.description: This team's `image-policy` catalogue and defaults, per RFC 0005.

catalog.description: This team's catalogue entries, merged into the cluster catalogue at resolution.

items.description:
One entry of `spec.features.imagePolicy.catalog`: a key, and the image patterns it permits.

**Carries no scope, no exception and no negation**, per RFC 0005's *A pattern set is a
union*: selecting more entries can only ever permit more, so an `except` field would be a
rule whose meaning depends on which other entries happen to be selected.

key.description: The short identifier a grant, an attribute, or the top-level `default` names.

patterns.description:
The image patterns this entry permits. Non-empty; parsed by `weebo-si-image-policy`, and
held here as the text an admin wrote so the CRD stays readable by `kubectl` and GitOps.

default.description: The entries a workspace of this team gets when it names none. May be empty, which means the platform set and this team's cluster-level default and nothing else.

items.description:
A short identifier for a catalogue entry, unique within the catalogue. Same rationale as
`CatalogKey` in `dwoc_pin` and `ProfileKey` in `network_profiles`: a key is never a
`{name, namespace}` pair, and never a bare `String` a team name could be passed as.

kubearmorPolicy.description: This team's `kubearmor-policy` catalogue and defaults, per RFC 0006.

catalog.description: This team's catalogue entries, merged into the cluster catalogue at resolution.

items.description:
One entry of `spec.features.kubearmorPolicy.catalog`.

Carries one [`TemplateRef`] directly rather than a `variants` list, unlike
[`crate::network_profiles::Profile`]: there is exactly one backend today, and the
variant-per-backend shape is deferred until a second one actually exists rather than
speculatively built now — RFC 0006's *Alternatives considered*.

key.description: The short identifier a grant, an attribute, or a resolved decision names.

templateRef.description: The `KubeArmorPolicy` object this entry copies its rule content from.

default.description: The runtime profiles a workspace of this team gets when it names none. May be empty: the cluster baseline applies either way.

items.description:
A short identifier for a runtime profile catalogue entry, unique within the catalogue. Never
a `{name, namespace}` pair — same rationale as `CatalogKey` in `dwoc_pin` and `ProfileKey` in
`network_profiles`.

networkProfiles.description: This team's `network-profiles` catalogue and defaults, per RFC 0004.

catalog.description: This team's catalogue entries, merged into the cluster catalogue at resolution.

key.description: The short identifier a grant, an attribute, or a resolved decision names.

variants.description: This profile's variants, at most one per [`Backend`].

items.description: One backend's rendering of a profile. A profile carries at most one variant per backend.

backend.description: Which dialect this variant is written in.

templateRef.description: The template object this variant copies `policyTypes`/`ingress`/`egress` from.

default.description: The profiles a workspace of this team gets when it names none. May be empty: the cluster baseline applies either way.

items.description:
A short identifier for a catalogue entry, unique within the catalogue. Never a
`{name, namespace}` pair — same rationale as `CatalogKey` in `dwoc_pin`.

A DNS-1123 label of at most 63 characters: it is interpolated into object names and label
values.

level.description:
A Pod Security Standards level.

**Lowercase on the wire, unlike every other enum in this CRD**, because these are upstream's
values: the same spelling goes into the `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce` label, and an
admin who writes `restricted` in a namespace label should not have to write `Restricted` here.

The variant order is the strictness order, `Privileged < Baseline < Restricted`, so `Ord`
answers "which is stricter" and [`Ord::max`] is "the stricter of the two".

warnLevel.description:
A Pod Security Standards level.

**Lowercase on the wire, unlike every other enum in this CRD**, because these are upstream's
values: the same spelling goes into the `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce` label, and an
admin who writes `restricted` in a namespace label should not have to write `Restricted` here.

The variant order is the strictness order, `Privileged < Baseline < Restricted`, so `Ord`
answers "which is stricter" and [`Ord::max`] is "the stricter of the two".

registryConfig.description: This team's `registry-config` catalogue and defaults, per RFC 0007.

catalog.description: This team's catalogue entries, merged into the cluster catalogue at resolution.

ecosystem.description: Metric label and CLI grouping only — never a branch.

key.description: The short identifier a grant or a namespace annotation names.

sources.description:
The objects this entry expands into: at least one, at most one per
`{kind, name, namespace}` triple.

items.description:
One object a catalogue entry expands into.

A catalogue entry holds a *list* of these rather than a single reference because one ecosystem
routinely needs two objects with different confidentiality: the `ConfigMap` holding the
registry URL, and the `Secret` holding the token it authenticates with.

templateRef.description: The object an admin authored, copied verbatim into each granted namespace.

default.description: The entries a namespace of this team gets when it names none. May be empty, which means this team mounts nothing by default.

items.description:
A short identifier for a catalogue entry, unique within the catalogue — the name a grant or a
namespace annotation uses. A newtype for the same reason [`crate::ProfileKey`] is one: a
registry key must never typecheck where a network profile key is expected.

identity.description: What this team's members are outside Kubernetes.

groupRefs.description:
Authentik group **names** — `AuthentikGroup.spec.name`, resolved by the upstream operator
against its own API, never against Kubernetes. Each is checked against
`spec.features.identity.authentik.allowedGroupRefs` before anything is created.

namespaceSelector.description: The namespaces that belong to this team.

key.description: The label key this expression tests.

operator.description: How `values` is compared against the label's value, if any.

values.description: The comparison values `operator` reads. Unused by `Exists`/`DoesNotExist`.

matchLabels.description: Every key must be present with exactly this value.

priority.description: Precedence when a namespace matches more than one team: lowest wins, ties break on name.

workspace.description: What each member gets deployed for them.

che.description: The Eclipse Che workspace application, as an Argo CD template rendered per person.

name.description: The cluster's registered name in Argo CD. Exactly one of `server` and `name` is required.

namespace.description:
The namespace, templated. Its rendered value is what `{USER_NAMESPACE}` binds to
everywhere else, so it is resolved first and cannot name that variable itself.

server.description: The cluster API URL. Exactly one of `server` and `name` is required.

mode.description:
Required when the block is present, per the chassis rule that a behaviour nobody wrote
down does not run: `Off` keeps the template without acting on it, which is how a team
stops provisioning for everybody without losing what it configured.

name.description: The `Application`'s own name, templated. Defaults to `{OBJECT_NAME}`.

project.description:
The Argo CD project, which is the outer fence this operator relies on rather than
reimplements. Checked against `spec.features.identity.che.allowedProjects`.

chart.description: A Helm chart name. Exactly one of `chart` and `path` is required.

path.description: A path inside a git repository. Exactly one of `chart` and `path` is required.

repoUrl.description:
The chart repository or the git repository. Prefix-checked against
`spec.features.identity.che.allowedRepoUrls`.

targetRevision.description: Chart version, git revision, or branch.

values.description:
The base Helm values every member of this team gets, templated. A person's own
`spec.che.values` is deep-merged over this.

Free-form, and the only free-form field in this crate — see [`crate::free_form`].

syncPolicy.description: Passed through verbatim — this operator has no opinion on how Argo syncs.

prune.description: Delete resources no longer in the chart.
